text.p: France's Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale was backing out of an agreement to turn the Europe's Airbus consortium into a unified corporation, Germany's Der Spiegel newsweekly said on Saturday.

Aerospatiale, going against an integration plan agreed in January, now wanted to keep the production plants of the four Airbus partners out of the restructured group, Der Spiegal said in an article due to appear on Monday.
Aerospatiale also wanted a Frenchman to take the helm of the new Airbus, the magazine said.

British Aerospace Plc and Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), a unit of car maker Daimler-Benz AG, sought to look outside the group for a successor to Airbus chief executive Jean Pierson, whose contract runs out next spring, Der Spiegel said.
The chairman of Airbus' supervisory board, former Daimler chief executive Edzard Reuter, told Der Spiegel he would resign if Aerospatiale continued to hold up the reorganisation.
"My patience is not unlimited," he said.
The loose Airbus consortium also includes Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA.

The integration plan would bring the partners' Airbus production, design and sales operations into a unified, listed company. The move is seen as crucial if Airbus is to develop its 500-passenger A3XX jumbojet and compete with industry leader Boeing Co..
DASA could not be reached for comment on Saturday.
